definitions.explanation: The Romance language spoken in Portugal, Brazil, and several other countries. In Japan, Portuguese has historical significance as one of the first European languages introduced through contact with Portuguese missionaries and traders in the 16th century. Brazil's large Japanese diaspora also means Portuguese-Japanese bilingualism is notable.

examples.japanese: ポルトガル{語|ご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
{彼女|かのじょ}はポルトガル{語|ご}とスペイン{語|ご}の{両方|りょうほう}が{話|はな}せる。
examples.english: She can speak both Portuguese and Spanish.

examples.japanese: ポルトガル{語|ご}は{世界|せかい}で{約|やく}2{億|おく}5{千万|せんまん}{人|にん}に{話|はな}されており、{主|おも}にブラジルとポルトガルで{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: Portuguese is spoken by about 250 million people worldwide and is mainly used in Brazil and Portugal.

notes:
Portuguese has had notable influence on Japanese vocabulary since the 16th century. Many Japanese loanwords come from Portuguese, including {天麩羅|てんぷら} (tempura, from 'tempero'), パン (bread, from 'pão'), and タバコ (tobacco).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ポルトガル{語|ご}{圏|けん}: Portuguese-speaking world
- ポルトガル{語|ご}で{話|はな}す: to speak in Portuguese
- ポルトガル{語|ご}の{通訳|つうやく}: Portuguese interpreter

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スペイン{語|ご}: Spanish — closely related Romance language also spoken in many countries
- ポルトガル: Portugal — the country (not to be confused with ポルトガル語 the language)
